candidate.name: Community-capped endorsements
candidate.formula: sum over communities of min(n[g,p], cap)

meta.verdict: Reduces antisemitic exposure in 1 of 3 fixtures: Concentrated harmful support. Costs: Concentrated ordinary support (Counterspeech exposure).
limitations: All sample labels await expert review.
Harmful items are abstract descriptions; the action model does not read text.
Behavior is a fixed probabilistic model, without live LLM calls.
Initial endorsements are authored fixtures, not empirical measurements.
The benchmark illustrates a mechanism under assumptions; it does not predict real-platform effects.
Five seeds show variability, not statistical significance.
Exploratory rules and caps were chosen after seeing results; only the pre-registered run is a test.

capped.name: Community-capped endorsements

scenarios.name: Concentrated harmful support
scenarios.description: Four harmful posts begin with nine supporters each in one network community. Ordinary and counterspeech controls have broad support.

feedback.text: Antisemitic exposure falls by 21.8 pp in every seed.
Ordinary engagement rises to 121%-134% of baseline.
Counterspeech exposure rises to 150%-150% of baseline.
Jewish community-life reach rises to 127%-127% of baseline.

scenarios.name: Concentrated ordinary support
scenarios.description: Ordinary posts and counterspeech begin with concentrated support. Harmful focus posts have broad support, exposing collateral effects.

feedback.text: No consistent change in antisemitic exposure (0.0 to 0.0 pp).
Counterspeech exposure drops to 50%-50% of baseline.

scenarios.name: Distributed harmful support
scenarios.description: Harmful, ordinary, and counterspeech focus posts have broad support. The cap may have less effect on harmful exposure.

feedback.text: No consistent change in antisemitic exposure (0.0 to 0.0 pp).
